title: A soft answer (Proverbs 15:1)
carry: a soft tongue breaketh the bone

cards: The text arrives at 9:40 at night. It's short, and it's sharp, and it ends with a period that somehow feels like a slammed door. A reply starts forming almost at once: accurate, cutting, impossible to argue with.
Sending it would be satisfying for a minute or two. Then the phone buzzes again, and it's worse, and now two people are awake and angry. Proverbs has a sentence for the moment before you hit send.

teach.b: Proverbs fifteen, verse one, in the King James words: "A soft answer turneth away wrath." The second half finishes the thought: grievous words stir up anger. Two roads side by side, and you can see where each one ends.
The Hebrew for soft here is rakh: tender, gentle. It doesn't mean silent, and it doesn't mean giving in.

teach.h: A SOFT ANSWER TURNETH AWAY WRATH.
teach.b: A soft answer still says something; it just says it in a way that lets the other person lower their guard. Later the book pushes further, with a picture that sounds almost impossible: a soft tongue breaketh the bone.
Gentleness can do what force can't. The Tanakh has a story that shows it. In the book of Judges, after a battle, the men of Ephraim come to Gideon furious: why didn't you call us to fight?

teach.h: GIDEON AND THE MEN OF EPHRAIM.
teach.b: Gideon could have fired back. Instead he answers by praising them: what have I done, compared with you? And the text says their anger toward him abated.
A quarrel ends in one sentence. Notice what Proverbs doesn't say. It doesn't promise a soft answer always works, or that anger is never deserved.
It sets the two roads side by side and lets you see where each usually ends. Harsh words feed a fire. Soft ones give it nothing to burn.

how: Jewish teaching on careful speech draws on verses like Proverbs 15:1, and the line is quoted at home and in the classroom when an argument starts to rise.

o: silent: choosing not to answer at all
soft: tender words that still say something
giving in: letting the other side win

games.q: a soft answer — tap the pairs.

s: a soft answer means saying nothing at all
a soft answer is still an answer: it says something, gently.
Proverbs also says a soft tongue breaketh the bone
Proverbs 25:15: gentleness doing what force can't.
Proverbs promises a soft answer always works
it observes which way things usually go; it makes no guarantee.

games.q: you're Gideon. after the battle, the men of Ephraim confront you, furious they weren't called. what do you do?
games.why: Gideon asks what he has done compared with them, and the text says their anger abated when he said that.

practice: Bring to mind a conversation that tends to get heated, a sibling, a coworker, someone at home, and hear the sharp thing they usually say.
Instead of the cutting reply, find one soft sentence that is still true, say it silently, and notice your shoulders as you do. If you pray, you can ask for a soft answer when it counts.

wordCard.voice: Rakh. Hebrew for soft: tender words that still say something, and turn anger away instead of feeding it. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: a soft answer, the opening words of Proverbs 15:1.

carryVoice: Your line: a soft tongue breaketh the bone. Soft isn't silent, and it isn't giving in. That's day eight hundred fifty.
